tools.name: search
tools.description: Search Trello for cards and boards by text.

params_schema.description:
Trello search is ACCOUNT-wide, not board-scoped.

Not BoardScoped on purpose: `/search` spans every board the token can see,
which is the point of a search. Restricting it would make it a worse
version of list_cards.

query.description: Text to search for in cards and boards
query.title: Query

partial.description: Match partial words too -- 'reno' finds 'renovation'. Trello's default is exact-word only.
partial.title: Partial

params_schema.title: SearchParams

return_schema.description: One search result -- a card, board or member.
return_schema.title: TrelloSearchHit

tools.name: get_token_link
tools.description: Turn your Trello API key into a ready-made authorize link, so you can get a token without hunting for anything on Trello's page.

params_schema.description:
Just the key -- the one thing the user definitely has.

Not BoardScoped and no token field: this runs BEFORE a token exists. Asking
for one here would be the circular request that made the Connect screen
unusable -- a field the user had no way to fill.

key.description: Your Trello API key -- 32 hex characters, from the API Key tab of your Power-Up at trello.com/apps/admin.
key.title: Key

params_schema.title: GetTokenLinkParams

return_schema.description:
A ready-made authorize link, plus whether the key behind it is real.

The whole point is that the user does not have to find anything on
Trello's page: they open this link, click Allow, and Trello hands them the
token. `key_status` is checked first so a dead key is caught here rather
than after a pointless round trip through the Allow prompt.
return_schema.title: TokenLink

tools.name: check_access
tools.description: Report what this connector can currently reach in Trello, and explain anything missing.

board.description: Board name, e.g. 'Client Work'. Omit when the credentials reach only one board.
board.title: Board

return_schema.description:
What the connector can currently reach, and why anything is missing.

The field set mirrors what `check_access` actually reports. It was
originally written around a single board (list_count, can_write) while the
handler reported across ACCOUNTS -- and pydantic drops undeclared keyword
fields silently, so the report rendered blank with no error anywhere. Named
for the facts the handler really has.
return_schema.title: AccessReport

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.description: List the files and links attached to a Trello card.

board.description: Board name, e.g. 'Client Work'. Omit when the credentials reach only one board.
board.title: Board

card.description: Card whose attachments to read (name or id)
card.title: Card

return_schema.description:
One attachment on a card.

`is_upload` distinguishes a file Trello stores from a link that merely points
somewhere: deleting the first destroys the only copy, deleting the second
only removes a reference. That difference matters enough to be a field.
return_schema.title: TrelloAttachment

`field_type` is carried because it DECIDES the write shape: a number goes in

tools.name: connect_account
tools.description: Connect a Trello account by saving its API key and token, after checking the pair actually works.

params_schema.description:
The credentials the user pastes on the Connect screen.

Not BoardScoped: this is the one action that runs BEFORE any board is
known, so asking which board to act in would be circular. The boards are
discovered FROM the credentials.

TWO fields, not one, because Trello access is a PAIR -- the key identifies
the app, the token identifies the user, and neither works alone.

key.description: Trello API key -- 32 hex characters, from the API Key tab of your Power-Up at trello.com/apps/admin.
key.title: Key

token.description: Trello token -- generated for that same key through Trello's Allow prompt. NOT the Secret shown under the key: that signs OAuth and cannot authorise a call.
token.title: Token

params_schema.title: ConnectAccountParams

return_schema.description: Outcome of connecting credentials -- what got connected, and what next.
return_schema.title: ConnectResult

board.description: Board name, e.g. 'Client Work'. Omit when the credentials reach only one board.
board.title: Board

card.description: Card to put the sticker on (name or id)
card.title: Card

remove.description: Set true to REMOVE this sticker from the card
remove.title: Remove

return_schema.description: Outcome of a write, phrased so the narrator can state what changed.
return_schema.title: WriteResult

board.title: Board

card.description: Card to vote on (name or id)
card.title: Card

member.description: Who votes -- defaults to the connected account
member.title: Member

remove.description: Set true to take the vote back

secrets.name: trello_credentials
secrets.description: Trello API key and token -- one 'key:token' pair per line, one line per account. Generate the key at trello.com/apps/admin (Power-Up -> API Key), then authorise your own account through Trello's Allow prompt to get a token for that key. A token reaches every board its owner can see.
